rule: Start the head with a sphere and add the lower jaw, then guidelines for the eyes and nose; keep the eyes on a separate layer to adjust spacing and size.
In profile the top of the ear is level with the start of the eyebrow and the bottom of the ear is level with the bottom of the nose; the ear is tilted, not vertical.
In profile the corner of the mouth is in line with the front of the eye, and the bottom lip aligns with the forehead.
In profile the angle of the nostril line is generally parallel to the angle of the mouth.
In the front view the distance from the brow line to the bottom of the nose is repeated below the nose to place the bottom of the chin.
In the front view the inner corner of the iris is in line with the corner of the mouth.
Common front-view errors are a face too large for the head, eyes too big or too wide, a forehead too small, and eyebrows too high.
